ghsa_summary: Claude Code command validation bypass allows arbitrary code execution via $IFS shell variable and short CLI flag parsing errors (CWE-77)
ghsa_description: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool. Prior to version 1.0.93, errors in parsing shell commands related to $IFS (Internal Field Separator) and short CLI flags allowed attackers to bypass the read-only validation mechanism and trigger arbitrary code execution. The regex validation used \S+ to match patterns, which failed to account for shell variables like $IFS that contain no spaces but expand to whitespace at execution time. This created a TOCTOU gap: commands were validated before shell expansion but executed after variable resolution. Eight distinct command execution bypasses were identified. Reliably exploiting this requires injecting untrusted content into a Claude Code context window. Fixed in v1.0.93.
poc_readme: PoC from Flatt Security research: Attack command: rg -v -e pattern$IFS.$IFS$HOME/.claude/projects$IFS--pre=sh. The $IFS variable passes regex validation (matches \S+) but expands to spaces at execution time, turning a single approved command into 'rg -v -e pattern . ~/.claude/projects --pre=sh'. The --pre=sh flag causes ripgrep to execute sh on each file as a preprocessor. Malicious payloads like $(touch /tmp/pwned) embedded in conversation history files get executed as shell scripts.

The naive regex-based sed expression validation failed to catch the 'w' (write) command in certain syntactic positions.

ghsa_description: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool. Prior to version 1.0.20, due to an error in command parsing, it was possible to bypass the confirmation prompt to trigger execution of untrusted commands. The vulnerability arises from improper input sanitization in how Claude Code handles whitelisted commands (specifically echo). By crafting a string that breaks out of the intended command context, an attacker can execute unintended shell commands with no user confirmation required. Reliably exploiting this requires injecting untrusted content into a Claude Code context window. Discovered by Elad Beber of Cymulate. Fixed in v1.0.20.

The attack leverages agentic context window content (project files, documentation, external APIs) as the injection surface.

description: SnakeYaml's Constructor() class does not restrict types which can be instantiated during deserialization. Deserializing yaml content provided by an attacker can lead to remote code execution. We recommend using SnakeYaml's SafeConsturctor when parsing untrusted content to restrict deserialization. We recommend upgrading to version 2.0 and beyond.
cwe:

The product receives input or data, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the properties that are required to process the data safely and correctly.
Attack patterns: attacker provides malformed or unexpected input to trigger unintended behavior.

The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid. Deserialization flaws allow an attacker to send crafted input that, when deserialized, results in arbitrary code execution, denial of service, or other malicious outcomes.
Attack patterns: attacker crafts serialized object with malicious payload -> application deserializes it without type checking -> arbitrary class instantiation -> code execution.
ghsa_summary: SnakeYaml Constructor Deserialization Remote Code Execution
ghsa_description: SnakeYaml's Constructor class, which inherits from SafeConstructor, allows any type be deserialized. Types do not have to match the types of properties in the target class. A ConstructorException is thrown, but only after a malicious payload is deserialized. High severity: lack of type checks during deserialization allows remote code execution.
poc_readme: A tiny project for generating payloads for the SnakeYAML deserialization gadget. Uses javax.script.ScriptEngineManager with java.net.URLClassLoader to load a malicious JAR from a remote URL. The attacker compiles malicious Java code into yaml-payload.jar and hosts it on a web server, then crafts a YAML payload that triggers class instantiation via SnakeYaml's Constructor.

description: Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.73 contains a potential Denial of Service (DoS) issue within the Bouncy Castle org.bouncycastle.openssl.PEMParser class. This class parses OpenSSL PEM encoded streams containing X.509 certificates, PKCS8 encoded keys, and PKCS7 objects. Parsing a file that has crafted ASN.1 data through the PEMParser causes an OutOfMemoryError, which can enable a denial of service attack. (For users of the FIPS Java API: BC-FJA 1.0.2.3 and earlier are affected; BC-FJA 1.0.2.4 is fixed.)

ghsa_description: In Spring Boot versions 2.7.0 - 2.7.17, 3.0.0-3.0.12 and 3.1.0-3.1.5, it is possible for a user to provide specially crafted HTTP requests that may cause a denial-of-service (DoS) condition. Specifically, an application is vulnerable when it uses Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux and org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-actuator is on the classpath. WebMvcTags.method() and WebFluxTags.method() populate the method tag directly from the raw request string without validating against known HTTP methods, allowing unbounded Meter instances to exhaust heap memory. CVSS 5.3 (Moderate).

description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.
cwe:
CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
The product does not properly control the allocation and maintenance of a limited resource, thereby enabling an actor to influence the amount of resources consumed, eventually leading to exhaustion of available resources.
Attack patterns: attacker sends requests designed to consume disproportionate server resources -> server allocates resources without proper limits -> resource exhaustion -> denial of service.
ghsa_summary: HTTP/2 Stream Cancellation Attack
ghsa_description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows clients to indicate to the server that a previous stream should be canceled by sending a RST_STREAM frame. Abuse of this feature is called a Rapid Reset attack because it relies on the ability for an endpoint to send a RST_STREAM frame immediately after sending a request frame, which makes the other endpoint start working and then rapidly resets the request.
poc_readme: CVE-2023-44487 (HTTP/2 Rapid Reset). Examples demonstrate starting many streams and immediately sending RST_STREAM frame to avoid reaching MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS. Example 1: Sending 10000 GET requests and sending RESET STREAM frames after each request immediately. Example 2: Sending 100000 POST requests with single packet attack technique.

description: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat.Tomcat from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.0-M10, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.15, from 9.0.0-M1 through 9.0.82 and from 8.5.0 through 8.5.95 did not correctly parse HTTP trailer headers. A trailer header that exceeded the header size limit could cause Tomcat to treat a single request as multiple requests leading to the possibility of request smuggling when behind a reverse proxy. Older, EOL versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.0-M11 onwards, 10.1.16 onwards, 9.0.83 onwards or 8.5.96 onwards, which fix the issue.

ghsa_description: BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches(CharSequence, String) will incorrectly return true for passwords larger than 72 characters as long as the first 72 characters are the same. The hashpw function in spring-security-crypto's BCrypt class hashes only the first 72 bytes of a password, so any password longer than 72 characters is validated based solely on its first 72 characters. Affected: all Spring Security versions before 5.7.16, 5.8.x before 5.8.18, 6.0.x before 6.0.16, 6.1.x before 6.1.14, 6.2.x before 6.2.10, 6.3.x before 6.3.8, 6.4.x before 6.4.4.
poc_readme: No standalone PoC repository found. The vulnerability is trivially reproducible: create two passwords that share the first 72 characters but differ afterward; BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches() returns true for both against the same hash. The patch commit includes a test case demonstrating that a 73-character password now throws IllegalArgumentException.
